questions.q: What does the `with` keyword guarantee when opening a file?
options: The file is automatically deleted after reading
with has no real effect — it's purely optional styling
The file is opened in read mode no matter what mode you specify
The file is automatically closed when the block ends, even if an error happens partway through
questions.explain: with ensures proper cleanup (closing the file) automatically, even if an exception occurs inside the block.

questions.q: What's the difference between opening a file with "w" versus "a"?
options: "a" overwrites the file; "w" appends to it
"w" overwrites the file's entire previous contents; "a" appends to the end without erasing existing content
"w" only works with JSON files, and "a" only works with text files
They behave identically in every case
questions.explain: "w" (write) mode erases and replaces the file's contents; "a" (append) mode adds new content to the end.

Reads JSON data out of a file
Converts a Python object into a JSON string in memory, not a file
Writes a Python object directly to an already-open file as JSON
questions.explain: json.dump() writes directly to an open file object, as opposed to json.dumps() which returns a string.

questions.q: What's the difference between json.dump() and json.dumps()?
options: dump() is for reading, dumps() is for writing
dumps() only works with lists, dump() only works with dictionaries
They are exactly the same function with two names
dump() writes directly to an open file; dumps() returns a JSON string in memory — the extra 's' means 'string'
questions.explain: The naming convention is consistent: functions ending in 's' (dumps/loads) work with strings; those without (dump/load) work with open files.

questions.q: Why would an AI engineering project commonly use json.dump() to save data to disk?
options: Because JSON files run faster than Python dictionaries
Because json.dump() is required to make any API call
Because most real data saved and loaded in AI projects — configs, cached responses, structured results — is JSON
Because Python cannot write plain text files, only JSON
questions.explain: The lesson highlights that configs, cached API responses, and structured results are typically stored as JSON files.
